issues.summary: Bare-file mode heuristic (dot/separator check) is brittle — misclassifies multi-arg unknown commands or fails for extensionless files.
issues.resolution: Replaced dot/separator heuristic with known-command exclusion: bare-file mode triggers only when args.Length==1 and the token is not a help flag, not a known subcommand, and does not start with '--'.

issues.summary: Source file decoded as strict UTF-8 only; Windows-1252 VBA exports would produce false ERROR_TOKEN counts.
issues.resolution: Added BOM-aware decoding: detect UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) and UTF-16 LE BOM (FF FE); try strict UTF-8; fall back to Encoding.Default (Windows-1252 on typical Windows VBA dev machine). R2 narrowed further: GetEncoding(1252) instead of Encoding.Default (deterministic across all locales). R3 (retry cap reached): simplified to BOM-first / Windows-1252-default with no try/catch, eliminating the silent-misdecode-on-valid-UTF-8-bytes concern entirely.

issues.summary: Schema-validation table in parse-failure-log.md missing rows for AddressOf, implicit-With .member / !key, named args, and empty positional args.
issues.resolution: Added rows for §5.6.4 AddressOf, §5.4.7 implicit-With leading .member and !key (H-C01/H-C02), §5.5 named args (H-D12), and §5.5 empty positional args (H-D08).

issues.summary: PrintUsage() did not document the parse subcommand or bare-file mode.
issues.resolution: Added parse usage lines, bare-file mode explanation, JSON output shape, and exit codes for parse to the usage text.

issues.summary: Encoding fallback still uses Encoding.Default which is locale-dependent.
issues.resolution: Replaced Encoding.Default with Encoding.GetEncoding(1252). Further improved in R3 by removing the try/catch approach entirely.

verificationRound3.note: Retry cap reached. R3 finding: UTF-8-first-then-fallback still silently misclassifies some Windows-1252 files. Fixed in-place at retry cap: simplified to BOM-first / Windows-1252-default (no try/catch). This eliminates the silent-misdecode concern without adding --encoding option. 244/244 tests pass.

issues.summary: No-BOM path still tried UTF-8 first — Windows-1252 bytes forming valid UTF-8 would be silently misclassified.
issues.resolution: Removed try/catch approach. New logic: BOM present → honour BOM; no BOM → Windows-1252 directly (GetEncoding(1252)). This is simpler and correct for Access VBA exports.
